title: Roadside-grass screw pressing, continuous grass-juice digestion, and digestate plant-use evidence (abstract-level extract)
license: Publisher page states exclusive copyright and no open license. UGent record says authors do not have permission to share data. This extract contains only a minimal abstract-level factual value and route statements; do not redistribute full article or supplementary data without permission.
geography: Roadside grass study by Ghent University and collaborators; exact sampling site/geography not given in accessible abstract
source_location: Publisher abstract; the full text is access-restricted. UGent bibliography lists the published version as UGent-only and states data cannot be shared.

units_and_basis.Nm3/t fresh matter: Normal cubic metres per tonne of fresh matter as printed in the abstract. Accessible abstract does not define whether the tonne basis is incoming roadside grass, juice, or another fresh-matter stream.

limitations: Abstract-only extraction; experimental conditions and underlying tables are inaccessible in the public publisher record.

The source reports biogas, not methane volume; methane fraction and upgrading recovery are not available from the abstract.
No methane fraction, grass/juice analysis, press recovery, reactor conditions, retention time, loading, replicates, uncertainty, or mass balance is available from the accessible record.

The publisher states the article is under exclusive copyright; the institutional repository says authors do not have permission to share underlying data. This staged abstract-level evidence is reference-only and no source data files are redistributed.

The digestate plant trial does not establish fertilizer product grade, nutrient-recovery efficiency, or GreenHub market acceptance. The abstract flags high electrical conductivity and potential allelopathic effects for grass-juice digestate.
